text:
maria: Quick sanity check — trying to mirror nova-13b weights from HF to our S3 registry and the final object shows a different checksum than HF. HF lists sha256, registry UI shows md5 mismatch. Anyone seen gzip/content-encoding toggles cause this?
ken: Can you paste the HF artifact URL and the S3 path? also which checksum field are you comparing (metadata vs object-etag)?
maria: HF tarball URL: https://huggingface.co/org/nova-13b/resolve/main/weights.tar.gz
S3 path: s3://redwood-artifacts/hf/nova-13b/v1/weights.bin.gz
I was comparing HF sha256 (from the release page) to our registry md5 shown in the UI.
sam: quick note — when objects are uploaded with content-encoding: gzip the S3 ETag/md5 can be different because it's the gzipped bytes. If HF computed sha256 of the uncompressed weights and we stored compressed, that explains it.
julie: Also sometimes HF provides checksums in different formats. Did HF's sha256 come from the file blob or from the release manifest?
maria: HF page shows sha256: 8b7f2d3a... (truncated). Our registry md5 displayed as 5d41402a...
ken: can you run a local checksum on the object after download and on the raw extracted file? small commands:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/hf/nova-13b/v1/weights.bin.gz ./weights.bin.gz
sha256sum weights.bin.gz
gzip -d weights.bin.gz
sha256sum weights.bin
md5sum weights.bin
```
That'll show whether HF sha256 was for compressed vs uncompressed.
maria: ran the above; output: sha256 of weights.bin.gz = 3f2a1c..., sha256 of weights.bin (decompressed) = 8b7f2d3a..., md5 of weights.bin = 5d41402a... so HF sha256 matches decompressed file.
sam: OK that matches the hypothesis. The registry ETag/md5 showing 5d41402a is md5 of uncompressed bob? weird — our upload pipeline might be recomputing md5 after decompressing or re-encoding. Which uploader was used?
maria: upload was via mirror job using origin-sync role (mirror-worker v2).
ingest-bot: mirror-job-1876 completed: src=hf://org/nova-13b/weights.tar.gz dest=s3://redwood-artifacts/hf/nova-13b/v1/weights.bin.gz mode=copy gzip-preserve=true checksum=sha256:8b7f2d3a...
ken: @maria can you grab the mirror job logs (mirror-worker) — we had a bug where content-encoding was set incorrectly during multipart copy, causing S3 to store both compressed and uncompressed blobs depending on part sizes. That can flip how the UI computes md5.
julie: Also reminder — our registry expects a digest field in metadata: digest:sha256=<hex>. If that's missing we fall back to ETag. Can you check object metadata?
maria: object metadata shows: {"content-encoding":"gzip","x-amz-meta-digest":""} (empty digest).
ci-bot: note — there is an open PR #4823 to populate x-amz-meta-digest during mirror.qa: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/4823
sam: action items: 1) fix mirror-worker to set x-amz-meta-digest to HF-provided sha256 at upload time, 2) ensure content-encoding is preserved and ETag not used as canonical digest in UI when digest header present.
ken: quick workaround: re-run a small post-process to set metadata on the existing object without rewriting content (copy-with-metadata). command:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/hf/nova-13b/v1/weights.bin.gz s3://redwood-artifacts/hf/nova-13b/v1/weights.bin.gz --metadata-directive REPLACE --metadata x-amz-meta-digest=sha256:8b7f2d3a... --content-encoding gzip
```
That will update metadata in-place (server-side copy).
maria: doing that now. pinging @sam to confirm digest value.
sam: confirmed sha256:8b7f2d3a... — go ahead.
julie: one more thing — before we declare ready for serving, run tokenizer sanity: some HF tokenizers have pad token at id 1 and our serving stack expects pad id 0 which caused off-by-one earlier. run a quick check on vocab.json and tokenizer_config.json.
maria: ran tokenizer check, found pad_token_id: 1 in tokenizer_config.json. I ran a mapping script to reindex pad->0 for our registry ingest and left a note in the artifact metadata (tokenizer-pad-fix: true).
ken: perfect. pls also add a short note in the artifact manifest: original_digest=sha256:8b7f2d3a..., registry_canonical_digest=sha256:8b7f2d3a..., compressor=gzip, tokenizer_pad=1->0 (mapped)
maria: added manifest note and re-ran the registry indexer. UI now shows digest sha256:8b7f2d3a... and md5 field empty. :white_check_mark:
sam: I'll open a small PR to populate digest during mirror-worker uploads and add a unit test for content-encoding handling. assign to me and ken.
ken: assigning PR review to @ken and @julie.
maria: thanks everyone. leaving a final checklist here: - post-copy metadata fix applied - tokenizer pad remapped and noted - PR for mirror-worker to land - follow-up: run model-load smoke on dedicated cluster (sam)
julie: slap on the staging canary once PR lands, then run smoke.
maria: noted. closing this thread unless someone sees additional issues. :slightly_smiling_face:
